newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh offers to hold peace talks with rebels.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh offers to hold peace talks with rebels.

text.p: The Bangladesh government on Monday offered to hold peace talks with tribal rebels in the southeastern Chittagong Hill Tracts, officials said.

The director of the government's special affairs division, Mashiur Rahman, made the offer in a letter to Hangsadhaza Chakma, a leader of the political wing of the rebel Shanti Bahini (peace force), the officials said.

Hangsadhaza also leads a "liaison committee" appointed by the Shantis, who have waged an armed campaign for political autonomy since 1973 in the 14,200 sq-km (5,500 sq-mile) Hill Tracts bordering India and Burma.

The letter, signed on November 9, follows the expiry of a truce between the government and the rebels on October 31. The letter proposed talks be held on November 23 at a mutually agreed venue in the Khagrachhari district of the hill tracts.
"A Shanti Bahini response is expected soon," one official told reporters.
The Shantis began fighting in 1973 after Bangladesh rejected their demand for autonomy. They also want some 300,000 Bengali-speaking settlers expelled from the region.
Officials say more than 8,500 people including rebels, soldiers and civilians have been killed in the insurgency, which has also forced thousands of tribal families to seek refuge in India.
